question: Why is prayer essential in the Coptic Orthodox life?
reference_answer: Prayer is described by the Fathers as converse and union with God: St. Clement of Alexandria calls it conversing with God and St. John Climacus calls it the converse and union of man with God, food of the soul and a source of virtues (Q896). Its effects include inflaming the soul with the love of God and imprinting a clear conception of God in the soul so that God abides in us (Q901, St. Basil).
evidence: p.31: '896. What is prayer? St. Clement of Alexandria says, Prayer is ... converse with God'; p.34: '901. What are the effects of prayer? First: The soul is inflamed with the love of God.'

question: How does the Coptic Orthodox Church explain the Lord's Prayer?
reference_answer: The Lord's Prayer is important because the Son of God Himself taught it to His disciples, so we pray to the Father with the words of our Advocate (St. Augustine, St. Cyprian, Q931). It is prayed in the plural ('Our Father') because God bids us love our neighbour and pray for others (Q932). Addressing God as 'Our Father who art in Heaven' means that as children of God we raise our hearts to heaven; the Only Son has numberless brethren (Q933).
evidence: p.67: '931. Why is the Lord's Prayer important? St. Augustine says, The Son Himself ... taught His disciples ... this Prayer'; p.68: '933. Why do we address God thus: Our Father who art in Heaven?'

question: What guidance does the Coptic Orthodox Church give for a daily prayer rule?
reference_answer: The Church arranges the Agpeya (canonical hours) at set hours of the day; the incarnation of the Word sanctifies time itself, so the believer keeps set times of prayer without despising time (Q921). Practical steps for prayer include focusing the inner gaze on God the heavenly Father, forgetting every creature when beginning to pray (St. Basil), and lifting oneself from earthly cares to heavenly thoughts (St. Ambrose) (Q902).
evidence: p.51: '921. The Agpeya prayers are arranged at certain hours of the day, so should a Christian adhere to a certain time for prayer?'; p.37: '902. What practical steps lead us to practice prayer? First: Focus your inner gaze on God'

question: What does the Coptic Orthodox Church teach about salvation?
reference_answer: After the fall God revealed His divine economy for salvation: one divine work of the Holy Trinity in which each Hypostasis has a distinct role (the Father gave His Son, John 3:16; the Son gave Himself, Gal 2:20; the Spirit declares what is Christ's, John 16:14) (Q329). Christ offered Himself as a sacrifice for everyone and offers His free salvation to all; our part is to use our free will to share in His sufferings and be conformed to His death, supported by communion of His Body and Blood (Q356).
evidence: p.262: '329. What is the divine economy for our salvation?'; p.280: '356. Is this salvation available to all people? The Lord Christ ... offered Himself as a sacrifice for everyone.'

question: What is faith, according to the Coptic catechism?
reference_answer: Faith is 'the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen' (Heb 11:1): what we hope for is a present reality experienced spiritually, generating peace and joy. St. Cyril of Jerusalem calls faith an eye that enlightens every conscience, and St. Augustine says 'believe that you may understand' (Q7).
evidence: p.35: '7. What is faith? Now faith is the substance of things hoped for ... St. Cyril of Jerusalem says, Faith is an eye that enlightens every conscience'

question: How does the death of Christ on the cross save us from sin, the curse and death?
reference_answer: St. Paul compares Christ to Adam, the head of humanity according to the flesh: Christ came from Adam's seed by His incarnation but became the head of humanity as the Almighty giver of grace, uniting us with Him as our Head through faith (Q355). He offered Himself as a sacrifice for everyone and offers His grace freely; our part is to choose to share in His sufferings and be conformed to His death (Q356).
evidence: p.279: '355. How does the death of the Lord Christ on the cross save us from sin, the curse, and death? The apostle Paul ... comparing Him to Adam'; p.280: '356. Is this salvation available to all people?'

question: What is the purpose of the church sacraments and how do they relate to each other?
reference_answer: The purpose of the sacraments is the work of the Holy Spirit preparing the Church as a bride for the everlasting wedding (2 Cor 11:2; Matt 25:1) (Q672). They are related because the Spirit gives the believer suitable gifts through each: baptism gives spiritual birth as a child of God, chrismation the indwelling of the Spirit, repentance and confession continual washing from sin, the Eucharist union with Christ, unction healing, and matrimony a church in the home (Q673, chapter introduction).
evidence: p.515: '672. What is the purpose of the church sacraments? ... prepares her for the everlasting wedding'; p.516: '673. What is the relationship between all the sacraments? ... a. In the sacrament of baptism ... b. After baptism ... holy Myron'; p.514 lists baptism, chrismation, repentance/confession, Eucharist, unction, matrimony.

question: What does the Coptic Orthodox Church teach about the Eucharist?
reference_answer: The Eucharist is the mystery of uniting the faithful with the Saviour by partaking of His Body and Blood given for us, so that the whole being, including the body, is sanctified (Q764). It is a sacrifice, known since the apostles (Heb 13:10; the Didache; the Fathers) (Q765), and the pinnacle of Christian worship: the believer goes to Golgotha and remembers Christ's death and resurrection not only in words but by partaking of His Body and Blood (John 6:55-57) (Q766).
evidence: p.589: '764. What is the mystery of communion in the eucharist? It is the mystery of uniting us the faithful with the Savior'; p.591: '766. Why is the Sacrament of the Eucharist considered to be the pinnacle of Christian worship?'

question: Why is baptism necessary according to the Coptic Orthodox Church, and what are its blessings?
reference_answer: Baptism is declared in the Creed ('one baptism for the remission of sins'); the candidate is immersed three times in the name of the Holy Trinity and is buried with Christ to die to the life of sin and enjoy the resurrected life, since no one can enter the kingdom unless born of water and the Spirit (Q676, Q141). Its blessings begin with the death of the old man: baptism washes away sins and slays the lusts (St. John Chrysostom) (Q678).
evidence: p.519: '676. What is the sacrament of baptism? ... immersed in water three times in the name of the Holy Trinity'; p.521: '678. What are the blessings of baptism? First: The death of the old man.'; p.146: '141. What is the purpose of baptism? ... We confess one baptism, for the remission of sins.'

question: Is it necessary to confess to a priest as well as repenting privately before God?
reference_answer: Yes. The goal of confession is to encounter God, the Physician of souls; whoever does not feel his sins will not feel the need for the Physician. St. Basil the Great says sins must be confessed to those entrusted with the stewardship of the mysteries of God (1 Cor 4:1), just as people of old confessed their sins to John the Baptist (Q743).
evidence: p.575: '743. Is it necessary to repent before God in our private rooms, and then again in the presence of the Father of Confession? ... St. Basil the Great says, it seems necessary that sins be confessed to those entrusted with the stewardship of the Mysteries of God'

question: What are the signs of true repentance in Coptic Orthodox teaching?
reference_answer: True repentance shows worthy fruit: St. Basil the Great says those turning from sin must bring forth fruits worthy of repentance (Q752). The repentant believer's obligations include thanking God for His mercy, admitting he is a sinner who cannot live the holy life without grace, forgiving those who sin against him, and fixing his heart on heaven and the eternal wedding (Q730).
evidence: p.579: '752. What are the fruits of true repentance? St. Basil the Great answers, the manner of repentance should be appropriate and worthy fruit be shown'; p.568: '730. What are the important obligations of the believer who repents? First: He or she thanks God ... Second: To admit that he is a sinner ... Third: To be merciful'

question: How should someone respond after falling again into the same sin?
reference_answer: St. Basil the Great teaches that falling into the same sin again shows the person is not yet purified of what lies beneath it: like cutting off a tree's branches while leaving the root, the same shoots will grow back. The one who wants to be purified must cut out the very first causes of the fault, for example strife and envy grow from a root of arrogance and love of human glory (Q756).
evidence: p.581: '756. What is required of the repentant person when he falls into the same sin again? St. Basil the Great answers ... It is as if someone cuts off the branches of a tree but leaves behind the root.'

question: Why is Holy Tradition important in the Coptic Orthodox Church?
reference_answer: Tradition (Greek paradosis) does not mean imitation but handing over something precious: one generation delivers the faith and another receives it (Q61). In the apostolic age, before the New Testament books were canonized, tradition was the only source of Christian faith, teaching and worship; the early Church received the Old Testament through it and read it with a Christian mind (Q63).
evidence: p.81: '61. What does the word tradition mean? In Greek ... paradosis ... it does not mean imitation'; p.82: '63. What was the role of tradition in the apostolic age? ... tradition was the only source of Christian faith, teaching, and worship.'

question: How does the Coptic Orthodox Church explain communion with the saints?
reference_answer: The saints of all generations are members of the Church: they are 'fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God' (Eph 2:19), including those who pleased God before Christ came, while the struggling Church on earth endures hardship as good soldiers of Christ (Q465). The Church honours them with feasts: of the Theotokos, the angels, St. John the Baptist, St. Mark and the apostles, the martyrs, and the patriarchs and monastic fathers and mothers (Q1085).
evidence: catechism1 p.380: '465. Are all the saints, across all the generations, members of the Church? ... fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God'; catechism2 p.247: '1085. What are the feasts of saints? a. Feasts of the Virgin ... e. Feasts of the martyrs'

question: Why does the Coptic Orthodox Church place such emphasis on fasting?
reference_answer: Fasting began in Paradise: God gave Adam and Eve one commandment, not to eat of the tree of knowledge, so that by obedience they would declare that their love for God transcends everything. St. Basil the Great says our first parents were driven out of Paradise for lack of fasting, so fasting is what brings us back into the kingdom, and it is a medicine of the soul against sin (Q1015).
evidence: p.159: '1015. Why does the believer need to fast? God ... gave the humans one commandment ... St. Basil the Great says, Fasting began in Paradise'

question: What is the spiritual purpose of fasting in the Coptic Orthodox Church?
reference_answer: Fasting serves first the acquisition of virtues (St. Jerome: fasting is not itself a virtue but the foundation of virtues); second, it motivates thanksgiving, because the one who fasts becomes aware of God's grace at work in him (St. Evagrius); third, it teaches appreciation of food as a blessing, so that the end of the fast is a time of rejoicing without indulgence (St. Basil) (Q1029).
evidence: p.169: '1029. What is the purpose of fasting? First. Acquisition of virtues: St. Jerome says, Fasting is not itself an absolute virtue, but the foundation of virtues. Second. Motivation to give thanks ... Third. Appreciation of food as a blessing'

question: How does fasting prepare us for spiritual warfare?
reference_answer: Christ our Commander fasted in the wilderness before confounding Satan, so we imitate Him as His soldiers. The Fathers knew the Church's fasts are seasons of the most intense demonic warfare, a sign of the terror that those who truly fast instil in demons; St. Augustine says that when the tempter intensifies his warfare we must fast so the body strives against worldly desires and the soul conquers in humility (Q1021).
evidence: p.162: '1021. How does fasting prepare us for spiritual warfare? In the temptation on the mountain in the wilderness, Christ our Commander in war fasted'

question: What is the Jesus Prayer?
reference_answer: The Jesus Prayer (or arrow prayer) is the believer's practice of repeating the name of Jesus often, in short prayers that can be recited at any time even during work, so as to keep his thought from distraction and live in constant communication with God, attaining prayer without ceasing (Q960).
evidence: p.103: '960. What is the Jesus Prayer? ... Being confident in the power of the name of Jesus, the believer repeats it often. This is what we call the Jesus Prayer.'

question: Why does God sometimes delay answering our prayers?
reference_answer: St. Basil the Great says God may delay so that our zeal and desire to approach Him are multiplied and so that we appreciate and guard the gift when we receive it, since what is received with effort is protected. St. Augustine adds that when God gives slowly He is showing us the value of His good things, not refusing them (Q900).
evidence: p.33: '900. Why does God sometimes delay answering our prayers ...? St. Basil the Great says, It may be that He delays answering a prayer so that your zeal and your desire to approach Him may be multiplied'

question: What does the word catechism mean?
reference_answer: Catechism is a Greek word meaning a summary of religious teaching, presented orally or in a book, of the principles and foundations of Christian teaching, generally in the form of questions and answers; it has been used since the apostolic age (Luke 1:4), and Fathers such as St. Cyril of Jerusalem and St. Gregory of Nyssa addressed catechumens in Catechetical Lectures (Q1).
evidence: p.15: '1. What does the word catechism mean? The word catechism is a Greek word that means a summary of religious teaching ... generally in the form of questions and answers.'

question: Who was St. Abanoub el-Nehissy?
reference_answer: St. Abanoub was a child martyr born in Nehissah in the city of Talkha in the 4th century to pious Christian parents who both died when he was 12, so that he was called 'the lamented boy'. Seeing churches destroyed and Christians persecuted, he prayed, and Archangel Michael appeared to him and guided him to confess his faith before the governor, promising he would be strengthened and healed through his sufferings until he received the crown of martyrdom.
evidence: p.33: 'ABANOUB EL-NEHISSY (The martyr) St. Abanoub was born in Nehissah, in the city of Talkha in the 4th Century ... He was only 12 years of age when both his parents departed'; p.34: 'God sent him Archangel Michael ... declare his Christian faith'

question: How did St. Moses the Black come to faith?
reference_answer: St. Moses the Black, born between 330 and 340 AD, was probably a slave of a sun-worshipping tribal chief who expelled him for his evil; he became the leader of a gang of robbers and killers. Yet he kept raising his eyes to the sun, believing it the true God and asking it to reveal itself; he heard a voice telling him to go to the monks of Scetis, went carrying his sword, met St. Isidore the priest of the Cells, and begged to remain so that God would save him as He saved Isidore.
evidence: p.249: 'MOSES, THE BLACK (The martyr) His Upbringing ... born between the years of 330 and 340 AD ... a slave of a head of a tribe that worshipped the sun'; p.250: 'he heard a voice telling him to go to the wilderness to encounter the monks of the Scetis ... St. Isidore'

question: Who was St. Mary the Egyptian?
reference_answer: St. Mary the Egyptian lived in the 4th and 5th centuries. Her story was told by Zosimus, a priest-monk who had lived 53 years in a Palestinian monastery and was sent to a monastery near the Jordan whose monks spent Lent in the wilderness; on his way back before the end of Lent he saw a figure he first took for a demon and realised it was a human being, which began his encounter with her.
evidence: p.146: 'MARY, THE EGYPTIAN, ST. St. Mary, the Egyptian lived in the 4th and 5th centuries AD, and her biography was told by a priest called Zosimus'; p.147: 'His Encounter with Mary the Egyptian: ... Fr. Zosimus saw from afar a ghost'

question: Who was St. Demiana and how was she martyred?
reference_answer: St. Demiana was born near the end of the 3rd century to Marcus, governor of El-Burullus, Zaafaran and the Saysaban valley in the Nile delta. She refused marriage and at 18 chose virginity, living with forty virgin companions in a house her father built. After torture, the leader ordered her beheaded together with all forty virgins; she was martyred on the 13th of Toba, and her body rests in the church built by Queen Helena near Bilqas.
evidence: p.555: 'DEMIANA AND THE FOURTY VIRGINS, SS. (The martyrs) ... Her father Marcus was a governor on El-Burullus'; p.556: 'On reaching the age of 18 years, she proclaimed ... her decision to live as a virgin'; p.558: 'ordered cutting her head off, together with all the heads of the other virgins ... She was martyred on the 13th of Toba'

question: search saint: Verena
reference_answer: St. Verena was a virgin from Garagous in the district of Qus (Qena). As a nurse and relative of St. Victor of the Theban Legion she went with the legion to Switzerland; after St. Maurice, St. Victor and the legion were martyred under Emperor Maximian she travelled to Agaunum for their relics, then lived as a hermit in a cave at Solothurn, serving the poor, fasting and praying, working miracles and counselling young girls.
evidence: p.320: 'VERENA, ST. St. Verena was a virgin of the town of Garagous in the district of Qus ... joined the military in the Theban Legion, which was sent to Switzerland ... hermit in a place called Solothurn'

question: Tell me about St. Rebecca and her five children.
reference_answer: St. Rebecca (Refqa) was a widow from Kemola in the district of Qus with five children: Agathon, Peter, John, Amon and Amouna. Archangel Michael appeared to them; during Diocletian's persecution she urged her children to hold fast to the faith. The governor placed them on iron beds over fire, but God sent rain to extinguish it and more people believed; finally they were all martyred.
evidence: p.10: 'REBECCA AND HER FIVE CHILDREN (The martyrs) ... a mother of five children: Agathon, Peter, John, Amon, and Amouna ... Kemola of the district of Q[us]'; p.11: 'When Emperor Diocletian ... St. Rebecca urged her children to hold fast'; p.12: 'placed St. Rebecca and her children on iron beds and ignited fire underneath them, God sent rain'

question: Who was St. Bishoy?
reference_answer: St. Abba Bishoy was born in Shansa in Menufyia around 320 AD, one of six brothers raised by their widowed mother; an angel chose him, though frail, saying 'the Lord's strength is made perfect in weakness'. In Scetis he memorised most of the Bible, loved the Book of Jeremiah so that he was called 'Bishoy the Jeremian', valued handwork, refused gold, and through his pure heart met and talked with the Lord Jesus Christ.
evidence: p.358: 'BISHOY, ST. ABBA ... born in Shansa, a village in the governorate of El-Menufyia, around the year 320 AD. He was one of six brothers'; p.359: 'The Book of Jeremiah had a special place in his heart ... he was called Bishoy the Jeremian'

question: Who was St. Anthony, the Father of the Monks?
reference_answer: St. Anthony is considered the father of the monastic family and founder of the monastic movement. He was born in Komn Al-Aros near Beni-Sweif around 251 AD to wealthy parents; in 269, hearing the Gospel 'sell what you have and give to the poor', he sold his inheritance, placed his sister Dios in a convent and lived in strict asceticism by the Nile, where an angel taught him to alternate prayer and handwork, before he withdrew to the inner wilderness.
evidence: p.196: 'ANTHONY, FATHER OF THE MONKS, ST. ... born in the village of Komn Al-Aros - Beni-Sweif around the year 251 AD ... In the year 269 AD ... If you want to be perfect, go, sell what you have'; p.197: 'An angel of the Lord appeared to him ... weaving palm leaves ... got up to pray'

question: Who was Pope Cyril I of Alexandria?
reference_answer: Pope Cyril I (Kyrillos), the 24th Pope of Alexandria, was called 'Cyril the Great' and 'the Pillar of Faith'. His name is linked to the great Christological conflict: he led the Council of Ephesus in 431 AD, which condemned Nestorius, patriarch of Constantinople, and he is counted among the outstanding fathers and theologians of the Church, to whom the patristic understanding of the Incarnation owes more than to any other individual.
evidence: p.501: 'CYRIL I, The 24th POPE OF ALEXANDRIA This pope was given the title Cyril the Great and also Cyril the Pillar of Faith ... led the 2nd Ecumenical Council in Ephesus in the year 431 AD, which condemned Nestor'

question: Who was St. Takla Haymanot?
reference_answer: St. Takla Haymanot the Ethiopian (1215-1313) is a pillar of Ethiopian monastic life. His father was the priest Tsega Zeab and his mother Egzie Haraya (Sarah), a pious childless couple who gave their possessions to the poor and freed their slaves. He was born on the 24th of Kiahk, baptised with the name Fish Hazion ('Joy of Zion'), and as an infant caused flour to flow from a cup so his mother could feed the poor during a famine.
evidence: p.218: 'TAKLA HAYMANOT, THE ETHIOPIAN, ST. ... lived during the years 1215-1313 ... His father, the priest Tsega Zeab'; p.219: 'born on the 24th of the month of Kiahk ... baptized, and called by the name Fish Hazion'

question: Who was St. Simeon the Stylite?
reference_answer: St. Simeon the Stylite was a saint of unique and unusual lifestyle admired by believers, non-believers and barbarians alike, honoured by Persians, Midianites and Ethiopians, and consulted by Roman emperors; his disciple Theodoret wrote his life and called him 'the Wonder of the World'. He lived 70 years and departed in 459 AD; the patriarch of Antioch with six bishops, army leaders and 6,000 soldiers came in procession for his funeral.
evidence: p.154: 'SIMEON, THE STYLITE, ST. Unusual and Amazing Personality ... His biography was written by his disciple Theodoret ... The Wonder of the World'; p.160: 'lived for 70 years ... departed to heaven in the year 459 AD ... the patriarch of Antioch came, together with six bishops ... and 6,000 soldiers'

question: Who was St. Barbara the martyr?
reference_answer: St. Barbara is a martyr famous in East and West; the Coptic Church keeps her feast on the 8th of Kiahk and the Western and Greek Churches on 4 December. She was born in Gamis near Leopolis in Nicomedia at the beginning of the 3rd century under Emperor Maximinus I; her pagan father Dioscorus, hating Christians and fearing corruption, shut her in a high tower filled with idols and entertainments, but contemplating the sun, moon and stars she praised their Creator.
evidence: p.298: 'BARBARA, ST. (The martyr) ... The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on the 8th of Kiahk ... born in the village of Gamis near the city Leopolis in Nicomedia ... Her father Dioscorus ... built for her a high tower'

question: Who was St. Paul the First Hermit?
reference_answer: St. Paul the First Hermit was born in Alexandria around 228 AD; after his father's death his brother Peter tried to seize the inheritance, and on the way to court Paul saw a rich man's funeral, despised the world, spent three days praying in a tomb, and was led by an angel to Mount Nimra near the Red Sea, where he lived about eighty years unseen, clothed in palm leaves, fed by a raven bringing half a loaf daily. St. Anthony the Great was led by God to find him.
evidence: p.382: 'PAUL, THE FIRST HERMIT, ABBA ... born in Alexandria around the year 228 AD ... his older brother Peter'; p.383: 'an angel appeared to St. Paul and guided him to the wilderness ... mount Nimra, near the Red Sea. There he lived for eighty years ... half a loaf of bread, which was carried to him by a raven'

question: Who was St. Abanoub, and how old was he when his parents died?
reference_answer: St. Abanoub el-Nehissy was a 4th-century child martyr from Nehissah in Talkha, raised by pious Christian parents; he was only 12 years old when both his parents died, and he grieved so long that he was called 'the lamented boy'.
evidence: p.33: 'He was only 12 years of age when both his parents departed to Paradise ... he was called the lamented boy'

question: What is prayer, and why does God sometimes delay answering it?
reference_answer: Prayer is converse and union with God (St. Clement of Alexandria, St. John Climacus) (Q896). God sometimes delays answering so that our zeal and desire for Him grow and we treasure the gift when it comes (St. Basil), and to show us the value of His good things rather than refusing them (St. Augustine) (Q900).
evidence: p.31: '896. What is prayer?'; p.33: '900. Why does God sometimes delay answering our prayers'

question: Why does the believer need to fast, and what is the purpose of fasting?
reference_answer: The believer needs to fast because fasting began in Paradise with God's one commandment; our first parents fell for lack of fasting, so fasting is the way back into the kingdom and a medicine for the soul (Q1015). Its purpose is the acquisition of virtues (fasting is the foundation of virtues, St. Jerome), motivation to thanksgiving, and appreciation of food as a blessing (Q1029).
evidence: p.159: '1015. Why does the believer need to fast?'; p.169: '1029. What is the purpose of fasting? First. Acquisition of virtues'

question: Who was St. Demiana, and on which day is her martyrdom commemorated?
reference_answer: St. Demiana was the daughter of Marcus, governor of El-Burullus in the Nile delta, born at the end of the 3rd century, who chose virginity with forty companions and was beheaded with them. She was martyred on the 13th of Toba.
evidence: p.555: 'DEMIANA AND THE FOURTY VIRGINS ... Her father Marcus was a governor on El-Burullus'; p.558: 'She was martyred on the 13th of Toba.'

history.content: Who was St. Moses the Black?
**St. Moses the Black** was a former slave and gang leader born between 330 and 340 AD who repented, went to the monks of Scetis, and became a monk under St. Isidore, later ordained a priest.

question: How did he die?
reference_answer: When the Barbarians came to attack the monastery, St. Moses, who knew it beforehand by the Spirit, urged the brethren to flee but stayed himself, saying he had long awaited the fulfilment of 'all who take the sword will perish by the sword' (Matt 26:52). Seven brethren stayed with him and the Barbarians killed them all; he was martyred on the 24th of Paona in 408 AD at the age of seventy-five (or eighty-five).
evidence: p.253: 'His Martyrdom: Then, it happened that the Barbarians came to attack the monastery ... All who take the sword will perish by the sword ... The Barbarians entered the monastery and killed them all ... on the 24th of Paona in the year 408 AD'

history.content: The Jesus Prayer is a short prayer in which the believer repeats the name of Jesus often, at any time and even during work, to keep his thought from distraction and live in constant communication with God.

question: What does St. Anthony say about practicing it?
reference_answer: St. Anthony says: 'If you sit in your cell, work with your hands, while repeating the name of Jesus. Hold it fast in your heart and mind and sing it with your tongue: My Lord Jesus, help me; I praise You my Lord Jesus Christ' (Q971).
evidence: p.114: '971. What does St. Anthony say about the practice of the Jesus Prayer? If you sit in your cell, work with your hands, while repeating the name of Jesus'

history.content: **St. Bishoy** was born in Shansa in Menufyia around 320 AD, one of six brothers; an angel chose him for God's service and he became a great monk of Scetis.

question: Why was he called 'Bishoy the Jeremian'?
reference_answer: Because the Book of Jeremiah had a special place in his heart: he memorised most of the Bible, and it was said that he used to see the prophet Jeremiah while reading his book, so he was called 'Bishoy the Jeremian'.
evidence: p.359: 'The Book of Jeremiah had a special place in his heart; that it was said that he used to see the prophet Jeremiah during his reading of his Book; that he was called Bishoy the Jeremian.'

history.content: Why is the Lord's Prayer important?
Because the Son of God Himself taught it to His disciples, so we pray to the Father with the words of our Advocate, as St. Augustine and St. Cyprian explain.

question: Why did Christ tell us to pray it in the plural?
reference_answer: Because God bids us to love our neighbour: we pray for fellow believers and non-believers alike, so our will harmonises with God's will that all be saved (1 Tim 2:4); even in his private room the believer prays in the name of the whole Church. St. John Chrysostom notes Christ said 'our Father', not 'my Father', offering supplication for the body in common (Q932).
evidence: p.67: '932. Why did the Lord Christ bid us to pray the Lord's Prayer in the plural? God bids us to love our neighbor, so we pray for fellow believers the same way we pray for non-believers ... St. John Chrysostom says ... He says not, my Father ... but, our Father'

history.content: **St. Takla Haymanot** the Ethiopian (1215-1313) is one of the pillars of Ethiopian monastic life, born to the priest Tsega Zeab and his wife Sarah.

question: What name was he given at baptism?
reference_answer: At baptism he was called Fish Hazion, meaning 'the Joy of Zion'; the name Takla Haymanot was given later.
evidence: p.219: 'The little child was baptized, and called by the name Fish Hazion, (meaning: the Joy of Zion)'; p.220: 'his name from now on would not be Fish Hazion, but Takla Haymanot'

question: من هو الأنبا موسى الأسود؟
reference_answer: القديس موسى الأسود وُلد بين سنة 330 و340م، وكان أسود اللون من قبائل البربر، عبدًا لشيخ قبيلة تعبد الشمس طرده لكثرة شروره فصار رئيس عصابة قطاع طرق. كان يخاطب الشمس كالإله الحقيقي طالبًا أن يعرّفه ذاته، فسمع صوتًا يرشده إلى رهبان برية شيهيت، فذهب حاملًا سيفه وقابل القديس ايسيذورس قس القلالي وطلب أن يخلصه الله، ثم لبس إسكيم الرهبنة وجاهد جهادًا عظيمًا.
evidence: p.116: '✞ موسى الأسود الشهيد نشأته ... ما بين سنة 330 و 340 م ... كان عبدا لشيخ قبيلة تعبد الشمس ... فسمع صوتا يرشده أن يذهب إلى هذه البرية ليلتقي برهبان برية شيهيت'; p.117: 'ألبسه إسكيم الرهبنة'

question: من هو مارمرقس الرسول؟
reference_answer: هو يوحنا الملقب مرقس، وُلد في القيروان بليبيا من أبوين يهوديين من سبط لاوي (أرسطوبولس ومريم)، وتعلم اليونانية واللاتينية والعبرية، وسكنت أسرته أورشليم وفتحت أمه بيتها للسيد المسيح. خدم مع بطرس الرسول ورافق بولس وبرنابا في رحلتهما الأولى، ثم ذهب إلى مصر وأسس كنيسة الإسكندرية بعد أن كرز في المدن الخمس الغربية، ودخل الإسكندرية حوالي سنة 60-61م، وكان أنيانوس أول مصري يقبل الإيمان.
evidence: p.195: '✞ مرقس الرسول نشأته هو يوحنا الملقب مرقس ... ولد القديس مرقس في القيروان'; p.196: 'أسس كنيسة الإسكندرية ... ودخل الإسكندرية عام 61 م'

question: من هو الأنبا بولا أول السواح؟
reference_answer: الأنبا بولا رئيس السواح وُلد في الإسكندرية حوالي سنة 228م؛ ولما أراد أخوه بطرس اغتصاب الميراث اتجه إلى القضاء، فرأى في الطريق جنازة غني فاحتقر العالم، ودخل قبرًا مهجورًا ثلاثة أيام، ثم أرشده ملاك إلى البرية الشرقية بجبل نمرة قرب البحر الأحمر حيث عاش أكثر من 80 سنة لا يرى وجه إنسان، يعوله الله بغراب يحمل نصف خبزة يوميًا، حتى التقى به الأنبا أنطونيوس بإرشاد إلهي.
evidence: p.1128: '✞ بولا القديس رئيس السواح ... ولد في مدينة الإسكندرية حوالي سنة 228م'; p.1129: 'أقام بجبل نمرة القريب من ساحل البحر الأحمر. عاش أكثر من 80 سنة ... غرابا بنصف خبزة كل يوم ... لقاء مع الأنبا أنطونيوس'

question: من هو الأنبا أنطونيوس أب الرهبان؟
reference_answer: القديس أنطونيوس يعتبره العالم أب الأسرة الرهبانية ومؤسس الحركة الرهبانية. وُلد في قمن العروس ببني سويف حوالي سنة 251م من والدين غنيين؛ وفي سنة 269م سمع في الكنيسة 'إن أردت أن تكون كاملًا اذهب وبع كل مالك ووزعه على الفقراء' فباع نصيبه وسلّم أخته ديوس لبيت العذارى، وعاش بجوار النيل بنسك شديد حيث علّمه ملاك أن يجمع بين العمل والصلاة، ثم سكن مغارة على جبل القلزم قرب البحر الأحمر، وتتلمذ عليه البابا أثناسيوس.
evidence: p.1377: '✞ أنطونيوس القديس أب الرهبان ... ولد القديس في بلدة قمن العروس التابعة لبني سويف حوالي عام 251م'; p.1378: 'سكن في مغارة على جبل القلزم شمال غربي البحر الأحمر ... البابا أثناسيوس الرسولي الذي تتلمذ على يدي القديس أنطونيوس'

question: من هي الشهيدة دميانة؟
reference_answer: الشهيدة دميانة وُلدت من أبوين مسيحيين تقيين في أواخر القرن الثالث، وكان أبوها مرقس واليًا على البرلس والزعفران بوادي السيسبان، وتعمدت وهي في عامها الأول. رفضت الزواج وفي سن الثامنة عشرة أعلنت عزمها على البتولية فبنى لها والدها قصرًا عاشت فيه مع صديقاتها العذارى الأربعين في حياة نسكية. ولما جحد والدها الإيمان أمام الإمبراطور وبّخته بشجاعة حتى تاب ورجع، ثم استشهدت مع العذارى.
evidence: p.847: '✞ دميانة الشهيدة والأربعون عذارى الشهيدات نشأتها ولدت من أبوين مسيحيين تقيين في أواخر القرن الثالث، كان أبوها مرقس واليا على البرلس'; p.848: 'قيام مرقس من السقوط ألهبت هذه الكلمات والدموع قلب مرقس'

question: لماذا يحتاج المؤمن إلى الصوم، وماذا يقول آباء الكنيسة عن الصوم؟
reference_answer: الله أعطى آدم وحواء وصية واحدة ألا يأكلا من شجرة معرفة الخير والشر، ليعلنا بصومهما أن حبهما لله يسمو فوق كل شيء. يقول القديس باسيليوس إن الصوم بدأ في الفردوس وإن أبوينا الأولين طُردا منه بسبب عدم الصوم، فالصوم هو الذي به ندخل إلى الملكوت، وهو دواء النفس للتخلص من الخطيئة (سؤال 1015-1016).
evidence: p.93: '1015. ما هي حاجة المؤمن للصوم؟ ... يقول القديس باسيليوس: الصوم في الفردوس عندما قال الرب لآدم ... فالصوم إذن هو الذي به ندخل إلى الملكوت ... 1016. ماذا يقول آباء الكنيسة عن الصوم؟'

question: ما هي أهمية الصلاة الربانية؟
reference_answer: يقول القديس أغسطينوس إن ابن الله نفسه علّم تلاميذه هذه الصلاة، فلنا رجاء عظيم ما دام لنا مثل هذا الشفيع الذي يلقننا ما نطلبه، وهي تعلمنا ممن نطلب وماذا نطلب. ويقول القديس كبريانوس إنها صلاة جميلة إذ نسأل الله بكلماته ونرفع إليه صلاة المسيح نفسه (سؤال 931). ويدعونا المسيح أن نصليها بصيغة الجمع لأن الله يدعونا إلى محبة القريب فنطلب لإخوتنا (سؤال 932).
evidence: p.40: '931. ما هي أهمية الصلاة الربانية؟ يقول القديس أغسطينوس: علم ابن الله تلاميذه ومؤمنيه هذه الصلاة ... 932. لماذا يدعونا السيد المسيح أن نصلي الصلاة الربانية بصيغة الجمع؟'

question: ما هو سر المعمودية وما هي بركاته؟
reference_answer: سر المعمودية يعلنه إيمان الكنيسة في قانون الإيمان؛ يغطس طالب العماد في الماء ثلاث مرات باسم الثالوث القدوس، ويقبل الدفن مع المسيح ليتمتع بالحياة المقامة إذ يموت عن حياة الخطية، لأنه لا يقدر أحد أن يدخل ملكوت الله ما لم يولد من الماء والروح (سؤال 676). ومن بركاته موت الإنسان القديم: تُغسل خطايانا وتموت الشهوات الجسدية كما يقول القديس يوحنا ذهبي الفم (سؤال 678).
evidence: p.490: '676. ما هو سر المعمودية؟ أولا: يعلن عن هذا السر إيمان الكنيسة ... ثانيا: يغطس طالب العماد في الماء ثلاث مرات باسم الثالوث القدوس'; p.491: '678. ما هي بركات المعمودية؟ أولا: موت الإنسان القديم'

question: لماذا لا تعاد المعمودية؟
reference_answer: لأن المعمودية هي ميلاد جديد روحاني؛ فكما يولد الإنسان جسديًا مرة واحدة هكذا يكون ميلاده الروحي، وإن سقط في خطايا يمارس التوبة التي تُدعى ميلادًا جديدًا (سؤال 710).
evidence: p.511: '710. لماذا لا تعاد المعمودية؟ لأن المعمودية هي ميلاد جديد روحاني، فكما يولد المرء جسديا مرة واحدة، هكذا يكون ميلاده الروحي'

question: ما هو سر الشركة في الإفخارستيا؟
reference_answer: هو سر اتحادنا نحن المؤمنين مع المخلص بتناولنا جسده ودمه المبذولين، فيتقدس كل كياننا حتى جسدنا لينعم بالمجد الأبدي (سؤال 764). والإفخارستيا عمل ذبيحي عرفته الكنيسة منذ العصر الرسولي (عب 13: 10؛ الديداكية؛ الآباء) (سؤال 765).
evidence: p.536: '764. ما هو سر الشركة في الإفخارستيا؟ هو سر اتحادنا نحن المؤمنين مع المخلص بتناولنا جسده ودمه المبذولين ... 765. هل الإفخارستيا عمل ذبيحي؟'
